methods.categorical_reading: Astra is a Type II split with vertex \(W_0-\Pi_{\rm tail}W_0\), \(\Pi_{\rm tail}\) the tail eigenprojector of the output covariance \(W_0\,\mathrm{Cov}(x)\,W_0^\top\); because the split sees the data only through that output covariance it is \(CO(m)\times GL(n)\)-covariant (Prop II.16(a), with \(C\) the centred input covariance). On layers with \(d_{\rm out}-\operatorname{rank}W_0\ge r\) the tail lies in \(\mathrm{coker}\,W_0\), \(A_0=0\), and the pointing collapses into the apex stratum \(\mathrm T_B\).

Its rank allocation by \(|W_0\odot\bar G|\) is a coordinatewise statistic.

The truncations are A2 sub-objects DyLoRA\(_b\hookrightarrow\)DyLoRA\(_{r_{\max}}\).

The \(\ell_1\) penalty lives on \(Q\), not on \(\Theta\): the slide \((BD^{-1},Dg,A)\) fixes \(\rho\) but rescales \(\|g\|_1\), so the sparsity it induces depends on the gauge.

Its ablation score is a function of the rank-one split of \(BA\), which the \(GL_r\) gauge does not fix.

methods.categorical_reading: AutoLoRA is a recipe whose output is LoRA\(_{r_\ell}\) with meta-learned ranks; during the search \(\rho=W_0+\sum_j\mathrm{softmax}(\beta)_jb_ja_j^\top\), and since each \(\mathrm{softmax}(\beta)_j>0\) can be absorbed into \(b_j\), the selection variables \(\beta\) lie entirely in the fibre of \(\rho\). They act only through the cometric (as per-component learning rates), so the thresholded rank depends on the gauge representative the bi-level dynamics picks, not on the update.
